parsed.rationale: The structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, meaning the two protocols share no common members. `HLSAVPlayerProtocol` (line 20, `HLSPlayer/Protocol/HLSAVPlayerProtocol.swift`) exposes AVFoundation-level playback controls (`currentTime`, `seek`, `seekableTimeRanges`, `rate`) suited to HLS streaming via AVPlayer, while `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` (line 34, `MP3Streamer/Playback/AudioEnginePlayerProtocol.swift`) exposes AVAudioEngine-specific concerns (`installRenderTap`, `makeRenderTapStream`, `scheduleBuffer`, `scheduleBuffers`, `removeRenderTap`, `eventStream`). Although both live in the `Playback` package and each declares `pause:()` and `play:()`, the surface overlap is two trivially-named methods out of a combined seventeen distinct slots, and even those two differ in signature (`play:()` vs `play:() throws`). Introducing a shared parent protocol would either force an inappropriate throws annotation onto the HLS path or weaken the Audio Engine contract, and would provide no meaningful code reuse given zero shared implementation.
